criteria.rationale: Examined the assumptions in the spec's Known gaps and Residual risks against the code. Verified facts: pose update replaces the binary by rename (maintenance.go:531), so the os.SameFile check detects it; the spawn suppresses CLI usage (cli.go:160), so in-process runs lose no telemetry; the apply compares the full digest (closeout_plan.go:317). Unresolved but accepted as risks: the root-resolution difference (F2), the unbounded per-run work of followups and the hand-declared route classes, all disclosed with follow-ups.

runInProcess checks cancellation before admission, after admission and after completion. Slots are released by the goroutine itself, panics included. Reran the suite with go test -race: it passed, including the concurrency and abandoned-slot tests.

The handoff is an additive omitempty field on the pose_closeout_state include_plan response; the existing execution_plan is unchanged. The catalog golden only gains description text. The in-process wrappers keep runCLI's error contract.

A non-zero exit returns 'pose <cmd> failed: <message>'. A deadline, a cancellation or a full slot set returns GateExecutionError with a cause and a cleanup note, never a verdict. A panic becomes a failed run.

The CLI registers suggest and followups in an init linked into the pose binary that serves MCP. The parity test compares the spawned built binary with the in-process wrapper. The handoff's argv was run against the CLI apply.

Examined the response shape, the catalog golden and the self-update path. The response change is additive. The in-process route is skipped when POSE_EXECUTABLE is set or the installed binary has been replaced, which keeps pose-mcp-server-survives-self-update R2. F2 is the only known divergence and cannot be reached by a root the server selects.

Reran the spec's tests with -race across the three packages, all passing. Checked CloseoutHandoff against cmdClosePlan's flags and the apply's digest comparison. Blocked, terminal and unknown-view plans get no handoff.

Examined the design against D1 and R1-R9. Running suggest and followups in process from the CLI's own registered command functions gives one source of results without a second implementation (R1, R8). The typed handoff, derived only from PlanCloseout's output, gives MCP a read-only closeout route that applies nothing (R3-R5). The route inventory, held equal to the catalog and to the governance-write risk class by tests, keeps writes at the four domain write points (R6, R7).

mappings.rationale: The ADR amendment records the route classes, the in-process admission rule and the typed handoff that D1 adopts, and that R8 requires to be recorded before the code.
Adds the required common-domain-and-cli-mcp-handoff-integration check that qualifies R1-R9 under -race.
Adjusts the check's run pattern (commit 99b18c04 drops the renamed handoff-target test) so the matrix runs the tests in the requirement trace.

criteria.rationale: Read the handoff paragraph in POSE.md:844 and in the scaffold dist/POSE.md:831: they are identical, and the pt-BR copies cover the same content. The text matches CloseoutHandoff's fields and conditions and the in-process admission rule. The ADR amendment matches the code.

B31 keeps results, errors and authority from one source: the CLI command function. The extracted wrappers count zero spawns. P04: the handoff states that apply takes no context flag and that the performer verifies context in the target root, which is an explicit limitation. MCP offers a read-only plan plus a typed handoff, and P15 parity is tested. Writes stay at the four admitted points. The gates and the delegate harness keep the process boundary.

Execution failures say whether the command started, ran in the background or was discarded, and that nothing was written. The handoff states required_inputs, its receipt path and its invalidation. Remediation is actionable.
Every trace test of R1-R9 matches the check's -run pattern, and the suite passed when I reran it.

Compared the change set's files with the spec's Artifacts list: they match. No closeout-applying MCP tool, scheduler or retry was added. Moving the semantics into the domain package is left as a declared follow-up.

Swept the fields of the changed MCP response: the handoff carries no filesystem path, secret or reviewer identity. Its argv is structured and executes nothing. The authority line is a hint and grants nothing. Only read-only commands are registered to run in process.

The smallest sufficient alternative, a registry of two existing command functions plus a derived handoff struct, was the one chosen; no new runtime or tool was added. The choice is invalidated if a registered command writes, or if followups' work becomes unbounded in practice; both are disclosed with follow-ups.

findings.action: Resolve the root as the CLI dispatcher does before an in-process run, or reject a root that is not a project root.
findings.rationale: An in-process run hands the command Store.Root as it is, while a spawned run starts in that directory and lets the CLI resolve the project root; a root that is a subdirectory of a project would resolve differently. No known path differs because the server selects project roots; declared in the spec's Known gaps.

findings.action: Count the delegate runner's spawns in CLISpawnAttempts (or a per-route counter), or narrow the counter's documentation to the runCLI/runCLIExit wrappers.
findings.rationale: The pose_delegate_* cli-wrapper routes start the POSE binary through defaultDelegateRunner without incrementing CLISpawnAttempts, which common_operation.go:54-56 documents as counting every attempt of a wrapper to start the POSE binary; the spawn measurement R9 asks for undercounts those routes.
